text: These lines in the sidewalk look messy. I'm smoothing them over.

speaker: fitz
text:
Wait. Those lines are on purpose. Concrete shrinks as it dries and hardens.
It's strong when squeezed, but weak when pulled. So that shrinking can crack it, anywhere.

speaker: fitz
text:
It cracks, but builders choose where. Each line is a groove about a quarter of the way down. A weak spot.
So the crack usually forms under the line, neat and straight, instead of wandering across.

speaker: gauge
text: Ooh, what else is built weird? Subscribe and let's find out.
